● As suspected — no .git folder exists, so the project isn't connected to any
  repo. This happens when you download a GitHub repo as a ZIP file (it strips
  the .git history). Here's how to reconnect it:

  Step 1: You need the GitHub repo URL. It'll look like:
  https://github.com/<your-username>/PS4PKGTool.git

  Step 2: Run these commands (once you have the URL):

  # Initialize a new git repo locally
  git init

  # Connect to your GitHub remote
  git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/PS4PKGTool.git

  # Fetch the remote history
  git fetch origin

  # Check what branches exist on remote (usually 'main' or 'master')
  git branch -r

  # Create a local branch tracking the remote (adjust branch name as needed)
  git checkout -b main origin/main

  # Now you're synced — make changes, then push normally:
  git add .
  git commit -m "Your changes"
  git push origin main

  The key insight: git fetch origin pulls all the commit history from GitHub.
  You're not re-uploading everything from scratch — your local files should
  match the latest remote state (since you just downloaded them), so after the
  checkout there should be no diff.

  ---
  What's your GitHub repo URL? I can run the commands for you right now.

     Plan: Manifest Caching Feature for PS4 PKG Tool

     Context

     Every launch, the app scans all PKG directories and calls Read_PKG() on
     every file (~5-30 seconds for large libraries). This is wasted time when
     the file set hasn't changed. The user wants a manifest cache that persists
     scan results, with a prompt on startup asking whether to load from cache or
     rescan.

     Files to Create

     1. PS4PKGTool\Utilities\PS4PKGToolHelper\ManifestHelper.cs

     Static class handling all manifest I/O. Contains:

     - ManifestEntry class — one row of PKG data (all 14 DataTable columns +
     FilePath + FileLastWriteTimeUtc)
     - ManifestData class — wrapper with SchemaVersion, CreatedAt,
     PkgDirectories, ScanRecursive, Entries[]
     - ManifestFilePath property → Helper.PS4PKGToolTempDirectory + 
     "manifest.json"
     - ManifestExists() → File.Exists(ManifestFilePath)
     - LoadManifest() → deserialize JSON, return ManifestData or null on error
     - ValidateManifest(manifest, appSettings) → checks schema version=1,
     directory set matches (order-independent), scanRecursive matches. Returns
     (bool, string reason)
     - SaveManifest(dataTable, verifiedPkgList) → iterate DataTable rows, look
     up File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc per PKG, serialize to JSON
     - BuildDataTableFromManifest(entries) → reconstruct the 14-column DataTable
     from manifest entries. Region strings mapped back to byte[] using same
     ImageConverter + Properties.Resources.* pattern as Main.cs lines 2038-2046
     - BuildPkgPathList(entries) → reconstruct List<string> of full file paths
     for VerifiedPs4PkgList
     - FilterValidEntries(entries) → remove entries where !File.Exists(path) or
     File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(path) > entry.FileLastWriteTimeUtc. Returns
     (valid, removedCount)

     JSON Schema:
     {
       "SchemaVersion": 1,
       "CreatedAt": "2026-07-13T...",
       "PkgDirectories": ["D:\\PS4"],
       "ScanRecursive": false,
       "Entries": [
         {
           "FilePath": "D:\\PS4\\game.pkg",
           "Filename": "game.pkg",
           "TitleId": "CUSA12345",
           "ContentId": "EP0001-...",
           "Region": "EU",
           "SystemVersion": "10.01",
           "Version": "01.00 [01.00]",
           "PkgType": "Fake",
           "Category": "Game",
           "Size": "25.34 GB",
           "Psvr": "",
           "Ps4ProEnhanced": "",
           "Ps5Bc": "",
           "Directory": "D:\\PS4",
           "Backported": "No",
           "FileLastWriteTimeUtc": "2026-01-10T15:30:00Z"
         }
       ]
     }

     Region stored as string (not byte[]) to avoid binary bloat. Reconstructed
     on load via ImageConverter.

     2. PS4PKGTool\Forms\Manifest Loader\ManifestLoaderPrompt.cs

     DarkUI dialog (DarkForm) with:
     - Title: "PKG Manifest Found"
     - Labels: "A cached PKG manifest was found from a previous scan." + entry
     count
     - Two DarkButton: "Load from Manifest" and "Scan from Directory"
     - public bool LoadFromManifest { get; private set; } — set by button clicks
     - Size ~420x180, CenterScreen, FixedSingle

     3. PS4PKGTool\Forms\Manifest Loader\ManifestLoaderPrompt.Designer.cs

     Designer partial class following the pattern in PKG Directory 
     Settings.Designer.cs.

     Files to Modify

     4. PS4PKGTool\Utilities\PS4PKGToolHelper\Helper.cs (+1 line)

     Add after the FinalizePkgProcess field (line 39):
     public static bool LoadFromManifest { get; set; } = false;

     5. PS4PKGTool\Program.cs (~30 lines changed)

     Modify ChooseStartupForm() (lines 88-92):

     ChooseStartupForm():
       1. If manifest exists AND directories configured AND manifest is valid:
          → Show ManifestLoaderPrompt dialog
          → If user chose "Load from Manifest": set Helper.LoadFromManifest =
     true, skip to Main
          → Else: Helper.LoadFromManifest = false, fall through
       2. Normal flow (unchanged): show PKG_Directory_Settings or Main based on
     settings

     Guard: only prompt if appSettings_.PkgDirectories.Count > 0 && 
     !string.IsNullOrEmpty(appSettings_.PkgDirectories[0]).

     When loading from manifest, always skip PKG_Directory_Settings and go
     directly to Main().

     6. PS4PKGTool\Forms\Main\Main.cs (~80 lines changed, 1 new method)

     6a. LoadPKGGridView() (line 1837) — add branch at top of BackgroundWorker
     DoWork:

     if (Helper.LoadFromManifest)
     {
         // Fast path: load from manifest
         var manifest = ManifestHelper.LoadManifest();
         var (validEntries, removedCount) =
     ManifestHelper.FilterValidEntries(manifest.Entries);
         PKG.VerifiedPs4PkgList = ManifestHelper.BuildPkgPathList(validEntries);
         DataTable dttemp =
     ManifestHelper.BuildDataTableFromManifest(validEntries);
         // Count PKG types (game, patch, addon, app, unknown)
         // Bind to grid via Invoke
         this.Invoke(() => { PostPkgLoad(isManifestLoad: true); });
         return;
     }

     6b. PostPkgLoad() (line 2100) — add optional parameter:

     private void PostPkgLoad(bool isManifestLoad = false)
     - If isManifestLoad: skip ExtractTrophyFile() call (it calls Read_PKG() on
     every file)
     - Everything else runs normally (filter menus, column visibility, BGM
     setup)

     6c. RunWorkerCompleted handler (line 2093) — add save after normal scan:
     bw.RunWorkerCompleted += delegate
     {
         PostPkgLoad();
         if (!Helper.LoadFromManifest)
             SaveManifestAfterScan();  // NEW
     };

     6d. New method SaveManifestAfterScan():
     private void SaveManifestAfterScan()
     {
         try {
             DataTable dt = PKGGridView.DataSource as DataTable;
             if (dt != null && PKG.VerifiedPs4PkgList.Count > 0)
                 ManifestHelper.SaveManifest(dt, PKG.VerifiedPs4PkgList);
         } catch (Exception ex) { Logger.LogError($"Manifest save failed: 
     {ex.Message}"); }
     }
     Must be called on UI thread (already in RunWorkerCompleted context).

     Edge Cases Handled

     ┌─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┐
     │            Scenario             │               Behavior                │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Files deleted since manifest    │ Filtered out silently, logged         │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Files modified since manifest   │ Filtered out (LastWriteTime mismatch) │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Directories changed in settings │ Manifest invalid → full scan          │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Corrupt/manifest JSON           │ Load returns null → full scan         │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Schema version mismatch         │ Validate fails → full scan            │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ No directories configured       │ Manifest prompt skipped               │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ Refresh/rescan from UI          │ Normal scan → manifest updated        │
     ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ First launch (no manifest)      │ Normal scan → manifest created        │
     └─────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────┘

     Verification

     1. Delete manifest.json, launch → normal scan, verify manifest.json created
     2. Relaunch → prompt appears → click "Load from Manifest" → grid loads
     instantly, all columns correct
     3. Relaunch → prompt → click "Scan from Directory" → full scan runs,
     manifest updated
     4. Delete a PKG file → relaunch → load from manifest → deleted PKG not
     shown
     5. Change directories in settings → relaunch → no prompt → full scan runs

  Changes Summary

  filter stale entries

  What: New — DarkUI dialog with "Load from Manifest" / "Scan from Directory"

  What: New — designer partial class

  What: ~35 lines — manifest check in ChooseStartupForm() before any form
  appears
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  File: Forms/Main/Main.cs
  What: ~75 lines — fast-path in LoadPKGGridView(), PostPkgLoad(isManifestLoad),

  SaveManifestAfterScan()

  How It Works

  1. First launch → normal scan → manifest saved automatically
  2. Next launch → manifest found → dialog appears:
    - "Load from Manifest" → grid loads instantly from JSON (no Read_PKG calls)
    - "Scan from Directory" → normal scan, manifest updated
  3. Stale files → filtered out automatically (deleted or modified since
  manifest)
  4. Directories changed → manifest invalidated → full scan without prompt
  5. Refresh from UI → always does full scan → manifest updated

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
  │                 Step                 │          Manifest load?          │

  │ Grid population (scan all PKGs)      │ Skipped — loaded from JSON       │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Trophy extraction                    │ Skipped                          │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ BGM extraction                       │ Skipped                          │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Filter menus + free space            │ Runs (no Read_PKG needed)        │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │ When user clicks a PKG row →         │ Still runs — reads just ONE PKG  │
  │ LoadPKGDetails()                     │ on-demand                        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘

  So loading from manifest only ever reads a PKG file when you actually click on
  it to view details — which is the intended behavior. Fast startup, details
  on-demand.

● Trophy extraction (ExtractTrophyFile) extracts .TRP files from each PKG to
  disk (TrophyTempFolder). During manifest load I skip this. Here's the real
  impact:

  ┌─────────────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┐
  │        Data         │  Manifested?  │   What happens on manifest load   │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Grid columns (title │ Yes — all 14  │                                   │
  │  ID, region, size,  │ columns in    │ Loaded instantly from manifest    │
  │ etc.)               │ JSON          │                                   │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
  │                     │               │ Previously extracted TRPs still   │
  │ Trophy .TRP files   │ No — they're  │ on disk from last full scan →     │
  │ (extracted to disk) │ binary files  │ work fine. New PKGs won't have    │
  │                     │               │ TRPs until next full scan         │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Trophy              │               │ LoadPKGDetails() reads the TRP    │
  │ icons/details       │ No — loaded   │ from disk. If TRP exists →        │
  │ (shown when you     │ on-demand     │ instant. If not → just won't show │
  │ click a PKG)        │               │  trophy data for that PKG         │
  └─────────────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┘

  In practice: the first time you do a full scan, all TRP files get extracted to
  disk. On subsequent manifest loads, those files are still there, so trophy
  details work when clicking PKGs. Only PKGs added after the last full scan
  would be missing trophy data.

● Yes — with one caveat. Here's the path when you click a PKG after manifest
  load:

  Click PKG row
    → LoadPKGDetails()
        → Read_PKG(selectedFile)           ← reads just ONE PKG (fast)
        → LoadTrophyInfo(ps4Pkg)
            → Checks disk: TrophyTempFolder\{ContentId}_{Type}.TRP
                → TRP exists?  → parses it → shows trophy list + icons ✅
                → TRP missing? → empty grid ❌

  LoadPKGDetails() calls Read_PKG() on the single selected file (not all files),
  so that's fine — it's instant. Then it just reads the pre-extracted .TRP file
  from disk.

  Bottom line: If that PKG was ever part of a full directory scan before, its
  TRP was extracted and trophy data will show. Only brand-new PKGs that never
  went through a full scan would be missing trophy data.

● Plan ready. Here's the summary:

  The update version is a web API call to Sony's servers — you can't do it
  during scan without blocking everything. So the plan is:

  1. Scan: Column starts empty (fast, no web calls)
  2. Post-scan: Background worker fetches update versions for all PKGs
  sequentially, updating cells as results arrive
  3. Manifest: Fetched versions are cached for instant load next time
  4. Each launch: Background refresh updates any changed versions

  This gives you fast startup + the update data fills in progressively.

● User approved Claude's plan
  ⎿  Plan saved to: ~\.claude\plans\smooth-cooking-backus.md · /plan to edit
     Plan: Add "Latest Update" Column to PKG Grid

     Context

     Currently, the game update version is only visible in the "PKG Update" tab
     (tabPage5) after selecting a single PKG. The user wants it as a column in
     the main grid to check hundreds of PKGs at a glance.

     The update check
     (PS4_Tools.PKG.Official.CheckLatestUpdateVersionAndMinFirmware(TITLEID)) is
     a web API call to Sony's servers — it's NOT a local lookup like PSVR/PS5BC
     (which uses a pre-downloaded JSON file). This is why the calls were
     commented out in Main.cs lines 1752 and 2035 — N sequential web calls
     during scan would be extremely slow.

     Approach: Deferred Background Fetch + Manifest Cache

     1. During scan: Column shows empty/"-" (no web calls, scan stays fast)
     2. After scan completes (both normal and manifest): Background worker
     fetches updates sequentially for all PKGs, updating grid cells as results
     arrive
     3. Manifest: Stores fetched update versions for instant load next time
     4. Staleness: Update versions are always checked fresh in background after
     each load — manifest data is a starting point that gets refreshed

     Files to Modify

     1. Main.cs — LoadPKGGridView() (~line 1903)

     Add column #14 "Latest Update" to the DataTable:
     dttemp.Columns.Add("Latest Update");
     Row addition gets empty placeholder:
     dttemp.Rows.Add(..., "");  // last param is Latest Update

     Also add grid column visibility config in the Invoke block (same pattern as
     PSVR columns at lines 2078-2081).

     2. Main.cs — PostPkgLoad() and new method

     After FinalizePkgLoadingProcess(), start a background worker that:
     - Loops through PKG.VerifiedPs4PkgList
     - For each PKG, calls Read_PKG() to get TITLEID
     - Calls
     PS4_Tools.PKG.Official.CheckLatestUpdateVersionAndMinFirmware(TITLEID)
     (returns tuple (version, minFirmware))
     - Updates the grid row via this.Invoke
     - Has a try-catch so one failed API call doesn't stop the rest

     New method: FetchAllUpdateVersions() — runs in BackgroundWorker, throttles
     calls if needed (short delay between calls to avoid rate limiting).

     3. Main.cs — UpdateDataGridViewColumnVisibility() (~line 2245)

     Add column index 14 visibility toggle bound to
     appSettings_.pkglatestUpdateColumn.

     4. Utilities/Settings/AppSettings.cs

     Add property:
     public bool pkgLatestUpdateColumn { get; set; } = true;

     5. Program.cs — CreateDefaultSettings() (~line 50)

     Add default setting line:
     pkg_latestUpdate_column=True

     6. Utilities/Settings/SettingsManager.cs

     Add parsing for pkg_latestUpdate_column in both Load and Save.

     7. Utilities/PS4PKGToolHelper/ManifestHelper.cs — ManifestEntry

     Add property:
     public string LatestUpdate { get; set; }

     8. ManifestHelper.cs — BuildDataTableFromManifest()

     Add "Latest Update" column to DataTable, populate from entry.

     9. ManifestHelper.cs — SaveManifest()

     Read "Latest Update" from DataTable row, write to entry.

     10. Forms/Main/Main.cs — SetDataGridViewCellStyle() (~line 2182)

     Add column 14 to center-aligned columns.

     Flow

     Scan completes → PostPkgLoad() → FinalizePkgLoadingProcess()
       → FetchAllUpdateVersions() [BackgroundWorker]
           → For each PKG:
               Read_PKG(file) → get TITLEID
               CheckLatestUpdateVersionAndMinFirmware(TITLEID) → web call
               Update grid cell via Invoke
           → On complete: SaveManifestAfterScan() (now includes update versions)

     Notes

     - CheckLatestUpdateVersionAndMinFirmware is in PS4_Tools.dll (external).
     The signature is (string updateVersion, string minFirmware). If it returns
     null/empty on failure, we show "-" or "N/A".
     - Rate limiting: add ~500ms delay between API calls to avoid Sony server
     throttling.
     - Internet check: first verify connectivity, skip if offline.
     - The manifest stores whatever the last fetched value was — it serves as a
     cache, gets refreshed each load.

     Verification

     1. Build and launch → normal scan → grid shows "Latest Update" column
     2. After scan, background worker fetches updates → cells populate
     progressively
     3. Close and relaunch → load from manifest → column shows cached values
     4. Wait for background refresh → values may update if Sony released new
     patches

❯ lets discuss.. dont code yet. how can we add features to drag and drop folder 
  into app? right now the app only load from directory set by users..           

  Thought for 10s (ctrl+o to expand)

● Good question. Here are the design decisions to think through:

  Where to drop

  The main form (Main.cs) already has the grid as the central element. Drop
  target could be:
  - The entire form — anywhere on the window
  - The grid area only — more intuitive, drop PKGs where they'll appear

  What to accept

  - Folders → scan for *.PKG inside
  - Individual .PKG files → add directly
  - Both

  The key design choice: merge vs temporary

  Option A — Temporary/Quick Look (Recommended)
  - Dropped folders/files are scanned and added to the current grid
  - Does NOT modify the configured directory settings
  - On next restart, only the saved directories are loaded
  - Use case: "I just downloaded a PKG to my desktop, let me quickly check it"

  Option B — Add to settings permanently
  - Dropped folders get added to appSettings_.PkgDirectories
  - Saved to Settings.conf, persist across restarts
  - Use case: "This is my new PKG folder, add it to my collection"

  Option C — Hybrid
  - Add to grid immediately
  - Show a small prompt: "Also add this folder to your saved directories?"
  - Best of both but adds friction

  Visual feedback

  - Change cursor on drag-over
  - Highlight the drop zone (border color change or overlay)
  - Show a small label: "Drop PKG files or folders here"

  ---
  My recommendation is Option A — drag-drop as a quick, non-destructive way to
  peek at PKGs without polluting saved settings. Users who want permanence can
  still use the directory settings form.

  Which approach do you prefer?

● Right — Option B it is, and yes, only scan the dropped folder. Here's the
  refined design:

  Flow

  User drops folder onto Main form
    → Accept only if it's a folder (or .PKG file)
    → If .PKG file: use its parent folder
    → Add folder to appSettings_.PkgDirectories (if not already there)
    → Save settings immediately
    → Scan ONLY that folder for new PKGs
    → Append new rows to existing grid (don't clear existing data)
    → Update filter counts + save manifest

  What changes

  ┌─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │            Piece            │               What it does                │
  ├─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Main.cs constructor         │ Set this.AllowDrop = true                 │
  ├─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Main.DragEnter              │ Check if dragged data is a folder/file →  │

● Build succeeded. 0 errors.

  What was added to Main.cs:

  Method: Main_DragEnter
  Purpose: Shows copy cursor when dragging files/folders over the form
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Method: Main_DragDrop
  Purpose: Extracts folder path (handles both folder and .PKG file drops), adds
  to saved directories, triggers incremental scan
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Method: ScanDroppedFolder(string path)
  Purpose: BackgroundWorker: scans only the dropped folder for *.PKG, validates
  magic bytes, reads metadata, appends new rows to existing DataTable, updates
  VerifiedPs4PkgList and counts, saves manifest, triggers update check

  Behavior:

  - Drop a folder → added to appSettings_.PkgDirectories, saved permanently,
  scanned immediately
  - Drop a .PKG file → its parent folder is used, same behavior
  - Drop non-PKG file → ignored
  - Duplicate folder → not re-added to settings, but still scanned for new PKGs
  - Duplicate PKG (already in grid) → skipped
  - After scan → manifest saved + update versions fetched for new entries

● Build succeeded. The fix: only the form itself has AllowDrop = true. In
  WinForms, drag events bubble up from child controls to the parent — so
  dropping on the grid or any other child control will bubble up to the form's
  DragDrop handler. The previous approach of setting AllowDrop on every child
  was actually blocking this bubbling.

● Build succeeded. Here's the new drop flow:

  Drop folder on app
    → Prompt 1: "Scan recursively?"
        [Yes] = include subfolders
        [No]  = this folder only
        [Cancel] = skip this folder

    → Prompt 2 (if not saved already): "Add to saved directories?"
        [Yes] = saved permanently, scanned on next launch
        [No]  = just scan this time

● The DarkDataGridView is a completely custom control (not a DataGridView
  subclass), so direct styling of properties like DefaultCellStyle or
  BackgroundColor isn't possible without modifying the DarkUI library itself.
  Here's what HAS been enhanced:

  Already enhanced:

  ┌──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │     Area     │                       What changed                       │
  ├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ All ~100     │ Replaced DarkMessageBox with clean custom AppMessageBox  │
  │ dialogs      │ (colored titles, auto-sized, consistent buttons)         │
  ├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Startup      │ 3-option Welcome dialog — clean title, bold labels,      │
  │              │ disabled buttons grayed out                              │
  ├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Drop folder  │ Single clean dialog — folder path + checkboxes +         │
  │              │ Scan/Cancel                                              │
  ├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Empty grid   │ Centered "Drop a PKG folder here" overlay with gray text │
  ├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Progress     │ Progress bar + counter during drop scans, matching       │
  │ feedback     │ normal scan format                                       │
  └──────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Constrained by DarkUI:

  The PKGGridView (DarkDataGridView) is a fully custom-painted control — it
  doesn't inherit from WinForms DataGridView at all. Properties like
  AlternatingRowsDefaultCellStyle, CellBorderStyle, GridColor, BackgroundColor,
  and CellFormatting don't exist on it. The grid's appearance is baked into the
  DarkUI DLL.

  The same applies to other DarkUI controls (DarkButton, DarkCheckBox,
  DarkSectionPanel, etc.) — they handle their own dark theming internally.

  What else I can do:

  - Detail panels (darkDataGridView2, TrophyGridView) — verify they're styled
  consistently

● Here's what I found in the DarkUI source:

  DarkUI Design Language

  Palette (from Colors.cs):

  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────┬────────────────────────┐
  │       Role       │    Value    │          Use           │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ GreyBackground   │ 60,63,65    │ Panels, form bg        │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ HeaderBackground │ 57,60,62    │ Section headers        │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ MediumBackground │ 49,51,53    │ Tab area, hover        │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ LightBackground  │ 69,73,74    │ Textboxes, buttons     │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ DarkBackground   │ 43,43,43    │ Pressed, inactive tabs │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ BlueSelection    │ 75,110,175  │ Selected tab, focus    │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ BlueHighlight    │ 104,151,187 │ Hover border           │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ LightText        │ 220,220,220 │ Active text            │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ DisabledText     │ 153,153,153 │ Inactive text          │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────┤
  │ DarkBorder       │ 51,51,51    │ Separators             │
  └──────────────────┴─────────────┴────────────────────────┘

  Patterns (from existing controls):
  - Flat design — no gradients, 1px borders only
  - 3 states — Normal / Hover / Pressed (DarkControlState enum)
  - No custom base class — each control inherits directly from WinForms
  - Custom OnPaint — every control does its own drawing
  - Font — Segoe UI, inherited, never explicitly set

  Tab drawing (from DarkDockGroup):
  - Tab height 24px, active tab fills BlueSelection, inactive DarkBackground
  - Tab separator: 1px DarkBorder vertical line
  - Active group gets a 2px BlueSelection divider line below tabs

  ---
  Proposed: DarkTabControl

  A DarkTabControl : TabControl following these patterns would look like:

  ┌──────────┬──────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Game    │  Patch   │                    │
  │  (blue)  │  (gray)  │                    │
  └──────────┴──────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  ← 2px
  BlueSelection line

  - Tabs: flat rectangles, no 3D bevels
  - Active tab: BlueSelection fill, LightText text
  - Inactive tab: DarkBackground fill, DisabledText text
  - Hover: MediumBackground fill
  - 1px DarkBorder separators between tabs
  - 2px BlueSelection underline below the active tab

  Want me to build it?

● Now add the rounded-path helper:

● Update(~\source\repos\DarkUI\DarkUI\Controls\DarkTabControl.cs)
  ⎿  Added 47 lines
      196          }
      197  
      198          #endregion
      199 +                                                              
      200 +        #region Helpers                                       
      201 +                                                              
      202 +        private static GraphicsPath GetTabPath(Rectangle rect,
          + int radius, bool allCorners)                                 
      203 +        {                                                     
      204 +            var path = new GraphicsPath();                    
      205 +            int r = radius;                                   
      206 +            int w = rect.Width - 1;                           
      207 +            int h = rect.Height - 1;                          
      208 +            int x = rect.Left;                                
      209 +            int y = rect.Top;                                 
      210 +                                                              
      211 +            // Top-left corner                                
      212 +            path.AddArc(x, y, r * 2, r * 2, 180, 90);         
      213 +            // Top edge                                       
      214 +            path.AddLine(x + r, y, x + w - r, y);             
      215 +            // Top-right corner                               
      216 +            path.AddArc(x + w - r * 2, y, r * 2, r * 2, 270, 9
          +0);                                                           
      217 +                                                              
      218 +            if (allCorners)                                   
      219 +            {                                                 
      220 +                // Right edge                                 
      221 +                path.AddLine(x + w, y + r, x + w, y + h - r); 
      222 +                // Bottom-right corner                        
      223 +                path.AddArc(x + w - r * 2, y + h - r * 2, r * 
          +2, r * 2, 0, 90);                                             
      224 +                // Bottom edge                                
      225 +                path.AddLine(x + w - r, y + h, x + r, y + h); 
      226 +                // Bottom-left corner                         
      227 +                path.AddArc(x, y + h - r * 2, r * 2, r * 2, 90
          +, 90);                                                        
      228 +                // Left edge                                  
      229 +                path.AddLine(x, y + h - r, x, y + r);         
      230 +            }                                                 
      231 +            else                                              
      232 +            {                                                 
      233 +                // Right edge (straight)                      
      234 +                path.AddLine(x + w, y + r, x + w, y + h);     
      235 +                // Bottom edge (straight)                     
      236 +                path.AddLine(x + w, y + h, x, y + h);         
      237 +                // Left edge (straight)                       
      238 +                path.AddLine(x, y + h, x, y + r);             
      239 +            }                                                 
      240 +                                                              
      241 +            path.CloseFigure();                               
      242 +            return path;                                      
      243 +        }                                                     
      244 +                                                              
      245 +        #endregion                                            
      246      }
      247  }

● Good idea. Here's the design approach:

  DarkGroupedListView

  A DarkUI.Controls.DarkGroupedListView — a custom control that displays items
  in collapsible groups.

  Visual design

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ ▼ EU (12)                                │ ← group header
  │   ├ CUSA12345 - Game Title               │ ← item row
  │   ├ CUSA67890 - Another Game              │
  │                                           │
  │ ▼ US (8)                                 │
  │   ├ CUSA11111 - US Game                   │
  │   ├ CUSA22222 - Another US Game           │
  │                                           │
  │ ▶ JAPAN (3)  (collapsed)                 │
  │                                           │
  │ ▶ ASIA (5)  (collapsed)                  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Architecture

  ┌─────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │     Feature     │                         Detail                         │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Base class      │ DarkScrollView (existing DarkUI scrollable base)       │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Group header    │ 24px tall, HeaderBackground fill, collapse arrow       │
  │                 │ (▼/▶), group title + count, LightText text             │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Item row        │ 20px tall, GreyBackground fill, indented 16px,         │
  │                 │ LightText text                                         │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Hover           │ Group header: MediumBackground, Item: LightBackground  │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Group by        │ User provides a Func<T, string> key selector, items    │
  │                 │ grouped automatically                                  │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Sort            │ Groups sorted alphabetically, items within groups      │
  │                 │ sortable                                               │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Collapse/expand │ Click group header to toggle, Colors.DarkBorder        │
  │                 │ separator between groups                               │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Selection       │ Single or multi-select items, BlueSelection highlight  │
  └─────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Group model

  // Simple: the control takes any objects + a grouping key function
  darkGroupedListView.SetItems(pkgList, pkg => pkg.Region);  // group by region
  darkGroupedListView.SetItems(pkgList, pkg => pkg.Category); // group by 
  category

  This would be a new file in DarkUI\Controls\DarkGroupedListView.cs. Want me to
  build it?

● Three approaches, ranked:

  Option 1: Separate tab (recommended)

  Tab: [PKG List] [Grouped View] [Trophy] [Images] ...
         ↑ DGV        ↑ New tab

  - Add tabPage8 with DarkGroupedListView dock-filled
  - Group-by dropdown in the toolbar: "Region", "Category", "PKG Type",
  "Directory"
  - Clicking a PKG in the grouped view syncs the selection back to the DGV tab
  (so detail panels still work)
  - Both views always available, zero config

  Pros: No workflow disruption. DGV stays for power-users (rename/move/RPI).
  Grouped view is purely for browsing. Easy to implement.

  Cons: One extra tab. Selection sync between views needs wiring.

  Option 2: Toggle on PKG List tab

  Tab: [PKG List]
         [Table ▾] ← toggle button
         ┌──────────────┐
         │ DGV or Grouped│
         └──────────────┘

  - Single tab, toggle swaps between flat DGV and grouped list
  - Simpler mental model — "this is where PKGs live"

  Cons: Detail panels (PARAM.SFO, trophy, entries) are wired to DGV selection.
  Toggling views breaks those bindings. More complex to implement safely.

  Option 3: Settings toggle

  - User picks DGV or Grouped in Program Settings
  - One view at a time, app remembers choice

  Cons: Buried in settings. Most users won't discover it. Unnecessary friction.

  ---
  My vote: Option 1. Both views side-by-side in tabs, no trade-offs. The grouped
  view gets a "Group by:" dropdown in its toolbar. Click a game in grouped view
  → switches to PKG List tab and selects that PKG in the DGV so all detail
  panels work as usual.

     Plan: Add Grouped PKG List View Tab

     Context

     The DGV shows all PKGs flat — hard to browse large libraries. Add a new
     "Grouped" tab with DarkGroupedListView that groups PKGs by a user-selected
     property (Category, Region, Type, Directory), with columns matching the DGV
     exactly.

     Files to Modify

     1. Copy updated DarkUI.dll

     - PS4PKGTool\Library.Core\DarkUI.dll ← from DarkUI repo build output

     2. Main.Designer.cs — Add tabPage8 + DarkGroupedListView

     Apply these additions:

     a) Field init (~line 296 area): Add:
     groupedListView = new DarkUI.Controls.DarkGroupedListView();
     tabPage8 = new TabPage();

     b) flatTabControl1.Controls.Add (~line 2188, after tabPage5):
     flatTabControl1.Controls.Add(tabPage8);

     c) Property block (before form properties, ~line 3247):
     // tabPage8
     tabPage8.BackColor = Color.FromArgb(60, 63, 65);
     tabPage8.Controls.Add(groupedListView);
     tabPage8.Location = new Point(4, 32);
     tabPage8.Name = "tabPage8";
     tabPage8.Size = new Size(951, 568);
     tabPage8.TabIndex = 7;
     tabPage8.Text = "Grouped";
     //
     // groupedListView
     groupedListView.Dock = DockStyle.Fill;
     groupedListView.Location = new Point(0, 0);
     groupedListView.Name = "groupedListView";
     groupedListView.Size = new Size(951, 568);
     groupedListView.TabIndex = 0;

     d) Field declaration (~line 3600):
     private DarkUI.Controls.DarkGroupedListView groupedListView;
     private TabPage tabPage8;

     3. Main.cs — Population + grouping logic

     a) Add method PopulateGroupedView() that mirrors the DGV columns:
     - Define 15 columns matching DGV exactly
     - Read from PKGGridView.DataSource DataTable
     - Call groupedListView.SetGroups() with the current grouping key

     b) Add "Group by" dropdown:
     - Add a DarkComboBox or ToolStripComboBox to choose grouping: Category,
     Region, PKG Type, Directory, Backported, Latest Update
     - On change → re-populate grouped view

     c) Call PopulateGroupedView() after:
     - PostPkgLoad()
     - ScanDroppedFolder() completion
     - Manifest load

     d) Selection sync:
     - When user clicks item in grouped view → select same PKG in DGV and switch
     to PKG List tab to show details
     - This keeps the existing detail panel logic working

     e) Context menu:
     - Wire contextMenuPKGGridView (the same menu) to
     groupedListView.ContextMenuStrip
     - The grouped view's SelectedItem Tag will hold the PKG file path, so
     existing handlers like CopyID_Click, DeletePKG_Click need to resolve the
     selected PKG from the grouped view

     4. Main.cs — Initialize empty grouped view

     In InitializeEmptyGrid() or Form1_Load empty-state path, also set up empty
     grouped view.

     Verification

     1. Build → run → scan PKGs → switch to "Grouped" tab → see PKGs grouped by
     Category
     2. Change "Group by" dropdown → list re-groups
     3. Click PKG in grouped view → switches to PKG List tab, details load
     4. Right-click in grouped view → same context menu as DGV works
     5. Drop a folder → grouped view updates with new PKGs
     6. Manifest load → grouped view populated from cache

  visibility, data). The DarkGroupedListView custom-paints headers with GDI+,
  while DarkDataGridView delegates to the native WinForms DataGridView header
  rendering.

  They'll never look identical because:

  - GVL headers = custom GDI+ drawing (hand-drawn)

  The proper fix: make DarkGroupedListView use a real DataGridView column header
  for rendering. I can embed a small hidden DGV, render just its header into a
  bitmap, and draw that. Or I can refactor GVL to actually wrap a DataGridView
  for the headers.

● No — there's no code in Program Settings.cs that sets button text or section
  headers at runtime. The issue is Visual Studio's Designer losing custom
  control properties when it regenerates the .Designer.cs file.

  This is a known problem with DarkUI's DarkSectionPanel and DarkButton — the
  Designer sometimes strips SectionHeader and Text because those properties use
  new to hide inherited members.

  The fix is in the DarkUI source — these properties need
  [DesignerSerializationVisibility(DesignerSerializationVisibility.Visible)] to
  tell the Designer to preserve their values. Let me check which ones are
  missing:

  Thought for 13s, ran 2 shell commands (ctrl+o to expand)

● Now ToShortPath() tries 3 strategies:

  1. 8.3 short name (instant) — X:\PKG\GAME\TRAIN~1.PKG
  2. Hardlink (instant, same drive) — creates temp link with safe ASCII name
  3. File copy (slow but always works) — copies to temp with sanitized name

  orbis-pub-cmd always receives a clean ASCII path.

✻ Baked for 58s

❯ what does this do                                                             

  Thought for 5s (ctrl+o to expand)

● When you run orbis-pub-cmd with a file like トライン 4：ザ・ナイトメア 
  プリンス.pkg, the tool can't read it because of Japanese characters and
  special symbols in the path.

  The fix: before passing the path to orbis-pub-cmd, it converts to a safe form:

  Before:  X:\PKG\GAME\トライン 4：ザ・ナイトメア プリンス.pkg
  After:   X:\PKG\GAME\TRAIN~1.PKG     ← 8.3 short name (instant)

  If 8.3 names are disabled on that drive, it falls back to creating a hardlink
  or temp copy with only ASCII characters. orbis-pub-cmd never sees the Japanese
  path.

✻ Cooked for 8s

❯ what is the command sample                                                    

  Thought for 6s (ctrl+o to expand)

● Without fix, orbis-pub-cmd receives:

  orbis-pub-cmd.exe img_file_list --passcode 00000000000000000000000000000000
  "X:\PKG\GAME\トライン 4：ザ・ナイトメア プリンス [Game] [v01.00].pkg"

  With the fix:

  orbis-pub-cmd.exe img_file_list --passcode 00000000000000000000000000000000
  "X:\PKG\GAME\TRAIN~1.PKG"

  The Japanese/Unicode path gets converted to its 8.3 short name before the tool
  sees it.

  "C:\PKG\temp_ps4pkgsafe.pkg" "C:\Output\Game Title"
